facts.statement: The holotype specimen MACN-PV-RN 1116 was discovered in 1995 by a team led by Dr. José F. Bonaparte.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Achillesaurus, MACN-PV-RN 1116, was discovered in 1995 by a team of the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales "Bernardino Rivadavia" led by Dr. José F. Bonaparte.

facts.statement: The genus name Achillesaurus refers to Achilles' heel because diagnostic features for these animals are found in that area.
facts.quote: Its genus name was chosen in reference to Achilles' heel, because diagnostic features are found there for these animals

facts.statement: Achillesaurus lived during the Santonian age of the Late Cretaceous in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Rio Negro, Argentina.
facts.quote: Achillesaurus is a genus of alvarezsaurid theropod dinosaur from the Santonian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Rio Negro, Argentina.

facts.statement: Achillesaurus measured approximately 2.7 meters in length and 1.5 meters in height, with an estimated weight of 30 to 50 kg.
facts.quote: Achillesaurus medía aproximadamente 2,7 metros de largo y 1,5 de alto, exhibiendo un peso estimado de 50 y 30 kg.

facts.statement: Only one specimen, the holotype MACN-PV-RN 1116, has been found, consisting of sacral vertebrae, four tail vertebrae, and the left femur, tibia, and ilium.
facts.quote: Sólo se ha descubierto un espécimen, el holotipo, MACN-PV-RN 1116, el cual consta de vértebras sacras, cuatro vértebras caudales, un fémur, una tibia y un isquion izquierdos.

facts.statement: Achillesaurus is classified within the family Alvarezsauridae alongside Alvarezsaurus and Patagonykus as a basal member.
facts.quote: Achillesaurus fue incluido, junto con Alvarezsaurus y Patagonykus, dentro de la familia Alvarezsauridae, siendo todos miembros basales.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that Achillesaurus might be a junior synonym of Alvarezsaurus because the two differ only trivially despite coming from the same formation.
facts.quote: However, Makovicky, Apesteguía & Gianechini (2012) argued that Achillesaurus might actually be a junior synonym of Alvarezsaurus, which, according to the authors, "is known from the same formation and from which it [i.e. Achillesaurus] differs trivially."

facts.statement: Achillesaurus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian period.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species name honors Professor Rafael Manazzone, an amateur paleontologist who assisted researchers with local knowledge.
rejected.quote: while the species name honors Professor Rafael Manazzone, an amateur paleontologist whose knowledge of Patagonian fossils and localities assisted the researchers on their field trips.
